data.name: Raffaela
data.long_meaning: From the Latin name Raphael, derived from the Hebrew name Rafael, meaning 'God has healed'. In Christian tradition, Raffaela is the female variation of Raphael, the name of an angel who healed the blind and restored sight to Tobias in the Old Testament.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes healing, compassion, and divine intervention.

in_hebrew.name: ראפאלה
in_hebrew.meaning: בת האל, אשה יפה, אהבה רפאים
in_hebrew.long_meaning: מקור השם הוא העברית 'רפא' - לרפא, ולאטי 'לה', ו-'אל' - לאל, ו-'ה' - ה' - האל. ראפאלה היא שם הבת לפי טעם עברי. זהו שם של אישה אשר נראית יפה. בפי האנוש אשה יפה, (אישה) אשר יפה, (אשה) שחורה, (אשה) (אדם) שחור.

in_greek.name: Ραφάελα
in_greek.long_meaning: Ο όρος Ραφάελα είναι σύνθετος, που αποτελείται από τις λέξεις 'ραφά' (ραφά, ραφάω) που σημαίνει «να θεραπεύσω, να ελπίζω», «να ελπίζω» και 'ηλα' (ἐλα, ἠλα, ἠλα, ἠλα, ἠλα, ἠλα) που σημαίνει «αίμα, σάρκα, κόρη». Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, ο όρος ραφάελα χρησιμοποιείται για να περιγράψει την κόρη του Θεού. Ο όρος ελατέρως χρησιμοποιείται για να περιγράψει την ελπίδα, την ανακούφιση. Ο όρος ραφάελα είναι ένα πιστό όνομα της ελπίδας.

in_latin.name: Raffaela
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Raffaela est a verbo Rapha, quod significat 'sanare, curare' et ab adjuncto 'la', quod significat 'filia'. In Ecclesia Christi, nomen Raffaela significat filiam Dei, quae est pulchra, et curam amoris, quae est spes, et solacio.

in_english.name: Raffaela
in_english.long_meaning: The name Raffaela is derived from the Hebrew words 'Rapha', meaning to heal, to cure, and 'la', meaning daughter. In the Christian tradition, the name Raffaela means God's daughter, who is beautiful, and care of love, which is hope, and solace. The name Raffaela is a faithful name of hope, and is often given to girls born into Christian families.

historical_references.reference: Raffaela was the name of a 13th century Italian saint known for her acts of compassion and charity, particularly towards the poor and the sick. She was also known as Raffaela of Palermo because she lived in Sicily.
historical_references.context: Raffaela was a laywoman, not a nun or a monk, who lived a life dedicated to serving others. She was particularly known for her care of the sick and the poor, often nursing them back to health. Her relics are still venerated in Palermo today.

historical_references.reference: Raffaela was also the name of a 16th century Italian painter, Raffaello Sanzio, who was born in Urbino, Italy. He is considered one of the greatest painters of the High Renaissance and is known for his mastery of various artistic techniques and styles.
historical_references.context: Raffaello Sanzio, commonly known as Raphael, was a highly influential painter who produced a large body of work in a relatively short period of time. He is particularly famous for his Madonnas and for his portraits, which were highly sought after by the European nobility. Raphael's work had a profound impact on the development of Western art.
